To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integration of dictionary resources with Web mining approaches, such as anchor text and search result, is effective for automatically extracting translation equivalents of query keywords not covered by standard dictionary.
the LiveTrans engine is an effective query- translation tool for digital libraries, and that it has the potential to be used in new applications for cross-language Web searching.

the proposed query translation approach can be used to automatically generate translations for queries that are not covered by standard dictionary resources and that it can improve the performance of CLIR services in digital libraries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to improve the performance of a query-translation engine for cross-lingual information retrieval in digital libraries.
the following questions: How can the query-translation engine be integrated into a cross-language information-retrieval system to enable cross-language queries to be processed?
the following two issues: how to improve the quality of cross-language query translation in digital library systems, and how to make use of Web resources for the purpose of query translation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper presents an innovative approach to the problem of query translation for cross-language digital library searching, which is a problem that is not only relevant to digital library research but also to the wider research community in cross-language information retrieval.
the approach proposed here is effective for cross-language query translations and is a promising solution to the problem of CLIR services in digital libraries.
the proposed approach has shown its feasibility in the context of digital libraries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, with the help of LiveTrans, the CLIR services can be more readily provided in digital libraries and Web searching.
the LiveTrans approach can be a good candidate to be used as a CLIR service in digital library systems.
, in addition to the dictionary-based approaches, the Web-based approaches have their own advantages, especially when the dictionary resources are insufficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a cross-language query translation service is feasible for digital libraries and that it is possible to build a cross-language search service in digital libraries that are not multilingual.
Web mining can be a useful and cost-effective approach for improving the coverage of CLIR systems.
a cross-language query-translation service can be effectively provided in a digital library system without having to build a multilingual digital library collection.
